metadata.title: Filter CSV Rows
metadata.description: Keep only the CSV rows whose ok cell is True and write them to a result CSV.

instructions.main: `data.csv` lives in the workspace with columns `name` and `ok`. Write `result.csv` with the header and only the rows whose `ok` cell is `True` (Ada and Linus).
steps: Read `data.csv` with `csv.reader`, capture the header via `next(reader)`, and keep rows where `row[1] == "True"` — cells arrive as strings.
Write `result.csv` with `csv.writer`: `writer.writerow(header)` then `writer.writerows(kept)`. Python's csv writer spells the boolean `True`.

hints.message: Read `data.csv` with `csv.reader`, keep the rows where `row[1] == "True"`, and write them back with `csv.writer`.
You are copying every row — only keep the ones where the `ok` cell is `True`: `kept = [row for row in reader if row[1] == "True"]`.
CSV cells arrive as strings — `row[1] == True` compares a string to a boolean and is never true. Compare against the string `"True"` instead.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: result.csv keeps only the rows whose ok cell is True.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: The result keeps exactly the True rows.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Write `result.csv` with the header and only the rows whose `ok` cell is `True` — Ada and Linus.
